newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks seen surging after IMF deal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks seen surging after IMF deal.

text.p: Pakistani stocks are likely to soar after the International Monetary Fund announced plans to reactivate a stalled $600 million standby loan, analysts said on Thursday.

"The IMF announcement, coupled with good corporate results in the past few weeks, will have a very positive effect on stock prices and market sentiment," Arif Habib, president of the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE), told Reuters.
"These announcements show an in-built strength of the stock market," Habib said, citing dividends of 20 to 80 percent declared recently by more than a dozen companies.
He said prices of several high-profile stocks shot up between five and 10 percent in the kerb market soon after word of the IMF deal emerged on Wednesday night.
The 100-share index rose 22.05 points, or 1.53 percent, to 1,467.29 at noon on the back of the IMF agreement.

"The news has proved a shot in the arm," said dealer Khalid Husain. "There is heavy buying by speculators and investors. Blue chips like Hub Power have surged passed previous resistance levels, but we expect profit-taking later in the day."
"The announcement will boost confidence of investors, particularly overseas buyers," said dealer Yasin Lakhani, former president of the KSE. "This is the time to buy."
IMF resident representative Shamsuddin Tareq told Reuters the fund would release two delayed tranches, worth about $80 million each, of the standby loan "as soon as humanly possible".

He said a visiting IMF mission had approved a stabilisation package announced on October 22 that included a devaluation of the rupee by 7.86 percent against the dollar, spending cuts, new taxes and a 10 percent increase in oil product prices.
Analyst Kalim Aziz of ING Barings said the IMF seal of approval might persuade the U.S.-based credit-rating agency Moody's Investors Service not to downgrade Pakistan's debt ratings.
"On the back of these developments, we call a buy on the market," he said. "We expect the market to easily rally up to the 1,500-1,550 (point) level before stabilising prior to the end of this year.
"We recommend market pivotals to ride the rally, particularly Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd, Hub Power Company, Fauji Fertiliser and Pakistan State Oil," Aziz said.
Dealer Ali Raza Mooney of Kausar Abbas Bhayani Securities said the agreement with the IMF had created a bullish mood.

The fund had been unhappy with Pakistan's repeated failures to meet many of its agreed targets and was not convinced that its budget for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) would effectively cut Islamabad's yawning fiscal and current account deficits.
